                                        ASIA ASSET FINANCE PLC
                             A Finance Company with a Golden Heritage — Muthoot Group Company
                    INTERIM FINANCIAL STATEMENTS — QUARTER ENDED 30TH JUNE 2026


Financial Review for the Quarter Ended 30th June 2026
Asia Asset Finance PLC (AAF), one of Sri Lanka's most trusted and fastest-growing non-banking financial institutions,
has delivered an exceptional first quarter for the financial year 2026/27, with a Profit Before Tax of Rs. 877.9 million,
up 197.8% year-on-year, and a Profit After Tax of Rs. 429.4 million, up 137.0% year-on-year. Total Assets grew to Rs.
60.42 billion, an increase of 12.3% over the quarter, while the Loan Portfolio expanded by Rs. 3.51 billion during the
quarter to Rs. 50.51 billion. These results reflect the continued strength of AAF's underwriting discipline, its
expanding branch footprint, and the enduring support of the Muthoot Group.

Key Highlights
  • Interest Income grew to Rs. 3.40 billion, up 85.4% YoY (30.06.2025: Rs. 1.83 billion)
  • Net Interest Income nearly doubled to Rs. 1.97 billion, up 120.0% YoY
  • Profit Before Tax increased to Rs. 877.9 million, up 197.8% YoY (30.06.2025: Rs. 294.8 million)
  • Profit After Tax rose to Rs. 429.4 million, up 137.0% YoY
  • Earnings Per Share more than doubled to Rs. 3.46, up 137.0% YoY (30.06.2025: Rs. 1.46)
  • NAV per Share improved to Rs. 41.89, up 31.1% YoY (30.06.2025: Rs. 31.96)
  • Return on Equity (annualized) strengthened to 34.4%, up from 18.7% a year ago
  • Return on Assets (annualized) improved to 3.0%, up from 1.8%
  • Net Interest Margin (annualized) expanded to 13.9%, from 10.6%
  • Asset quality continued to strengthen: Gross NPA Ratio improved to 7.5% (from 12.5%) and Net NPA Ratio
      improved to 4.2% (from 6.6%)
  • Capital remains well above regulatory thresholds, with Tier 1 Capital Adequacy at 18.96% (minimum 8.5%)
      and Total Capital Adequacy at 18.85% (minimum 12.5%)
  • The Company's share price closed the quarter at Rs. 59.10, up 44.1% YoY from Rs. 41.00

Significant Developments During the Quarter
Asia Asset Finance PLC — Quarter: 1 April 2026 to 30 June 2026

1. Branch Network Expansion
During the quarter under review, the Company opened five (5) new branches, expanding its island-wide network.
The new branches are as follows:
  • Nelumkulam
  • Omanthai
  • Padiyathalawa
  • Uppuweli
  • Mandur
With this expansion, the total branch network of Asia Asset Finance PLC stood at 120 branches as at 30 June 2026.

2. Opening of Training Centre
The Company opened a new training centre in Kurunegala during the quarter, in line with its ongoing investment in
staff development and capacity building.

3. Recommendation of Final Dividend
The Directors of Asia Asset Finance PLC have recommended the payment of a final dividend for the year ended 31
March 2026, as follows:



Class of Share                                            Dividend per Share                Total Amount (Rs.)

Ordinary Shares                                                Rs. 0.57                       Rs. 70,791,454

Preference Shares                                              Rs. 0.70                       Rs. 28,978,960




With sustained profitability momentum, improving asset quality, a well-capitalised balance sheet, and continued
network expansion, Asia Asset Finance PLC enters the remainder of FY2026/27 well positioned to build on this strong
start to the year.

 Flows), whereby operating activities, financing activities and investing activities have been recognised. Cash and Cash Equivalents comprise short term, highly
 liquid investments that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value. The cash and cash
 equivalents consists of cash in hand, balances with banks, placements with banks, money at call and short notice.

 FINANCIAL REPORTING BY SEGMENT

 As per the provisions of Sri Lanka Financial Reporting Standard, SLFRS- 8, the operating segments of the company have been identified based on the product and services offered by the Company of which level of risk and rewards is significantly different from one
 another. Top management of the company considers the operating results and conditions of its business segments in their decision making process and performance evaluation. Types of products and services from which each operating segment derives its revenues
 are described as follows.

 An operating segment is a component of the Company that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses, including revenues and expenses that relate to transactions with any of the company’s other components. All operating
 segments’ operating results are reviewed regularly by the Senior Management to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and to assess its performance, and for which discrete financial information is available.



 Segment results that are reported to the Senior Management Personnel and the Board of Directors include items directly attributable to a segment as well as those that can be allocated on a reasonable basis.

 Types of products and services from which each operating segment derives its revenues described as follows;
 Lease & Hire-purchase - This segment includes Leasing and Hire Purchase products offered to the customers.
 Loans - This segment includes Loan products offered to the customers
 Gold Loans - This segment includes Gold Loan products offered to the customers
 Investments - This segment includes treasury investments
 Other business - This segment includes all other business activities that engaged other than above segments.

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS



  01. The Interim Financial Statements are in compliance with the Sri Lanka Accounting Standard -

      LKAS 34: Interim Financial Reporting and the provisions of the Companies Act No. 7 of 2007 and

      provide the information as required in terms of Rule 7.4 of the Colombo Stock Exchange.

  02. The company has adopted consistent accounting policies and methods of computation as
      disclosed in the Annual Report for the year ended 31st March 2026.

  03. The Interim financial statements of Asia Asset Finance PLC for the period ended 30th June , 2026

      (including comparatives) were approved and authorized for issue on 28th July 2026 in accordance

      with a resolution of the board of directors on 28th July 2026.

  04. The presentation and classification of the financial statements for previous periods have been
      amended where relevant for better presentation and to be comparable with those of the current
      period.

  05. Impact Due To Current Economic Condition

      The Company has taken the following measures to ensure it continues its operations as a going
      concern.


      • Focus on asset backed lending
      • Strict credit evaluation to minimize credit risk
      • Restructure/reshedulment of stressed loans due to current adverse market conditions
      • Additional financing to minimize liquidity risk
      • Managing operational cost


      Based on proactive analyses and our operating model, financial strength of the company and the

      backing of the group, the management is confident that the company has no impact to its

      business continuity and expects to manage the economic challenges effectively
